In Christian theology, this condition inherited from Adam and Eve's expulsion from Eden was shaped significantly by Augustine of Hippo — what is it called?
Original sin: Christian doctrine about human nature.
An economist who began as a Madrid city councillor in 2004, he's led Spain's Socialist Workers' Party and, since 2022, presided over Socialist International — which prime minister is it?
Pedro Sánchez: Prime Minister of Spain since 2018. Sánchez began his political career in August 2004 as a city councillor in Madrid, before being elected to the Congress of Deputies in 2009.

Head of the Catholic Church for nearly 32 years — the longest verified reign in history — this pontiff convened a council that defined papal infallibility before declaring himself a 'prisoner' after Rome's capture in 1870 — who was he?
Pope Pius IX: Head of the Catholic Church from 1846 to 1878.
This ideology holds that humans split into groups ranked as inherently superior or inferior, based on supposedly inherited and shared traits — what is it called?
Sparked by an 1835 revolt against a Mexican president's new centralizing constitution, this sovereign nation lasted barely a decade before joining a much larger union — what was it?
Republic of Texas: Country in North America (1836–1846)
This U.S. Army officer led E Company's assault on the Belgian town of Foy after the siege of Bastogne was broken, and later served as the American governor of a Berlin prison — who is he?
A native of Zanzibar, she became Tanzania's first woman president in 2021 after ascending from the vice-presidency on her predecessor's death. Who is she?
Samia Suluhu Hassan: President of Tanzania since 2021. A native of Zanzibar, Suluhu served as a minister in the semi-autonomous region from 2000 to 2010.
Nicknamed both "the Blond" and "the Drunkard," this son of Suleiman the Magnificent saw Cyprus and Tunis conquered but suffered a famous naval loss at Lepanto — who was he?
Selim II: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1566 to 1574.
Eldest daughter of King Amalric, this 12th-century ruler stood by her unpopular husband Guy of Lusignan even as her leprosy-stricken brother struggled to secure her succession — who is she?
Sibylla, Queen of Jerusalem: Crusader ruler from 1186 to 1190.

Defined by a one-man police state, forced agricultural collectivization, and a sweeping cult of personality, this set of Soviet policies held sway from 1927 until the dictator's death in 1953 — what is it called?
Stalinism: Political and economic policies implemented by Joseph Stalin.
Led by a man who declared himself the younger brother of Jesus Christ, this 1850s Chinese theocratic state waged a 14-year war against the Qing dynasty — what was it?
Taiping Heavenly Kingdom: Theocratic monarchy in China (1851–1864)
A Whig historian famed for his prose, he both wrote a seminal "History of England" and played a major role in shaping India's education policy — who was he?
Thomas Babington Macaulay: British historian and politician (1800–1859)
What is this — “1938 spree killing in Japan”?
Tsuyama massacre: 1938 spree killing in Japan. It is the deadliest shooting by a lone gunman in Japanese history.
This American private equity investor and retired naval officer completed the Explorers Grand Slam and then dove to the deepest point of all five oceans during a 2018–19 expedition. Who is he?

In June 2014, forces captured the cities of Mosul and Tikrit, prompting Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki to call for a national state of emergency that parliament refused to grant — which conflict was this?
War in Iraq (2013–2017): Armed Conflict in the Middle East.
A social worker shaped by the 1960s and the Occupation of Alcatraz, she became the first woman elected Principal Chief of the Cherokee Nation — who is she?
Wilma Mankiller: Cherokee Nation chief and activist (1945–2010)
Once called 'perhaps the most famous singer alive' in much of Africa, this Senegalese star helped develop the mbalax genre and even served as his country's Minister of Tourism — who is he?
Youssou N'Dour: Senegalese politician and musician (born 1959)
Who among these was born first?
George Grove (born 1820) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four. Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
Which one below was born first?
Jan Hus (born 1369) is the earliest of the four. Hus is considered to be the first Church reformer, even though some designate the theorist John Wycliffe.
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Annie S. D. Maunder is an astronomer. As sole author, she also devised with her husband, Edward Walter Maunder, the butterfly diagram for sunspots.
Pick the mathematician from these four.

William James Sidis is a mathematician. Born to Boris Sidis, a prominent psychiatrist, and Sarah Mandelbaum Sidis, a physician, Sidis demonstrated extraordinary intellectual capabilities from infancy.
What is the atomic number of Tellurium?
Tellurium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Te and atomic number 52.
What is the atomic number of Manganese?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.
In what year was David Attenborough born?
David Attenborough: Sir David Frederick Attenborough ( AT-ən-bər-ə; born 8 May 1926) is an English broadcaster, natural historian, and writer.
In what year was Eratosthenes born?
Eratosthenes eventually became the chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria.
In what year was Michael Faraday born?
Michael Faraday: Although Faraday received little formal education, as a self-made man, he was one of the most influential scientists in history.
In what year did Carlo Acutis die?
Carlo Acutis: Acutis was canonised on 7 September 2025, alongside Pier Giorgio Frassati.
In what year did Srinivasa Ramanujan die?
Srinivasa Ramanujan Iyengar (22 December 1887 – 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
In what year was Uncertainty principle discovered?
Uncertainty principle: The uncertainty principle, also known as Heisenberg's indeterminacy principle, is a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics.
S.P. Korolev Rocket and Space Corporation Energia

Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. Approximately 60 countries across four continents have flown the MiG-21, and it still serves many nations seven decades after its maiden flight.
Zinc: Pfizer. Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In which country is Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker?
Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker: United States. It has a narrower fuselage and is shorter than the 707.
Who is credited with discovering Roentgenium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Roentgenium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Roentgenium (German: [ʁœntˈɡeːni̯ʊm]) is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rg and atomic number 111.
Who is credited with discovering 4 Vesta?
4 Vesta: Heinrich Wilhelm Olbers. Vesta (minor-planet designation: 4 Vesta) is one of the largest objects in the asteroid belt, with a mean diameter of 525 kilometres (326 mi).
Who is credited with discovering Lysosome?
Lysosome: Christian de Duve. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.
People with this anxiety disorder dread places they feel they can't escape — crowds, queues, public transit — and in severe cases may become unable to leave home at all. What is it?
Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder characterized by symptoms of anxiety in situations where the person perceives their environment to be unsafe with no way to escape.
Found on every continent but Antarctica and almost always monogamous breeders, which bird family unites ducks, geese, and swans under one scientific name?
Anatidae are the biological family of water birds that includes ducks, geese, and swans.

Once classified as bacteria and originally called archaebacteria, this domain of mostly single-celled prokaryotic organisms turns out to be the ancestral lineage from which eukaryotes evolved — which domain of life?
Archaea (ar-KEE-) is a domain of organisms.
One of the first grains ever domesticated, this cereal crop was cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9000 BC and later spread throughout Eurasia by 2000 BC — name the grain?
Barley (Hordeum vulgare), a member of the grass family, is a major cereal grain grown in temperate climates globally.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
One of only two elements liquid at room temperature, this reddish-brown, pungent-smelling element takes its name from the Greek word for 'stench.' What element is it (symbol Br)?
Bromine is a chemical element; it has symbol Br and atomic number 35.
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy and a prodrug of morphine, which opiate treats mild-to-moderate pain and is often paired with paracetamol?
Codeine is an opiate and prodrug of morphine mainly used to treat pain, coughing, and diarrhea.

Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flesh,' this breakdown product of muscle and protein metabolism is released into the bloodstream at a rate depending on a person's muscle mass — name the substance?
Creatinine (from Ancient Greek (kras) 'flesh') is a breakdown product of creatine phosphate from muscle and protein metabolism.
A colorless, volatile liquid (CH2Cl2) with a sweet, chloroform-like odor, it's slightly polar, mixes with many organic solvents but not water, and is widely used as a solvent — what is it?
Dichloromethane (DCM, methylene chloride, or methylene bichloride) is an organochlorine compound with the formula CH2Cl2.
This English physician created the world's first vaccine, targeting smallpox, and in doing so coined the very term 'vaccine' — derived from the Latin for 'pustules of the cow.' Who was he?
Edward Jenner (17 May 1749 - 26 January 1823) was an English physician and scientist who pioneered the concept of vaccines and created the smallpox vaccine, the world's first vaccine.
This flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of just two species cultivated for their alkaloid-rich leaves — what is its scientific name?
Erythroxylum coca is a species of flowering plant in the family Erythroxylaceae.

Species in the stinging genus Solenopsis are sometimes confused with unrelated weaver insects in Southeast Asia that share their reddish color and painful bite — what's the common name for this group?
Fire ant are several species of ants in the genus Solenopsis, which includes over 200 species.
Caused by abnormalities in the genome, this category of health problem may arise from a single faulty gene, many genes, or a chromosome abnormality — what is the general term?
Genetic disorder is a health problem caused by one or more abnormalities in the genome.
Designed in the late 1950s as a replacement for the piston-engined E-1 Tracer, this twin-turboprop U.S. Navy aircraft provides carrier-based early warning radar coverage. Name the aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.

Fox-sized and found on every continent but Australia and Antarctica, these primitive ornithischian dinosaurs are known for odd teeth — canine-like tusks plus cheek teeth built for chewing. What's this family?
Heterodontosauridae is a family of ornithischian dinosaurs that were likely among the most basal (primitive) members of the group.

Literally meaning 'below mania,' this psychiatric condition brings a non-contextual elevation of mood along with increased energy, irritability, and impulsivity, but without the psychotic features of full mania — name this condition?
Hypomania (literally "below mania" or "less than mania") is a psychiatric condition of abnormally heightened mood and increased energy that is less severe than mania.
Native to Africa and Eurasia, which group of opportunistic canid predators includes the black-backed, side-striped, and golden species?
Jackal are canids native to Africa and Eurasia.
This Columbia economist won the Nobel in 2001 and famously skewers his laissez-faire colleagues as "free-market fundamentalists" — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz (born February 9, 1943) is an American New Keynesian economist, a public policy analyst, political activist, and a professor at Columbia University.
This American economist served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, later led the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning a professorship there in 2026 — who is he?
Larry Summers (born November 30, 1954) is an American economist.
This Chinese computer engineer turned science-fiction writer won the 2015 Hugo Award for his novel The Three-Body Problem, and has also claimed China's Galaxy Award a record nine times. Who is he?
Liu Cixin (pinyin: Li Cxn,; born 23 June 1963) is a Chinese computer engineer and science fiction writer.

Living from about 6.2 million years ago until roughly 4,000 years ago, this extinct relative of modern elephants is distinguished by its large, spirally twisted tusks and cold-weather adaptations like a thick fur coat — name the animal?
Mammoth is a member of the extinct elephantid genus Mammuthus.
Home to a relativistic plasma jet stretching nearly 5,000 light-years from its core, this giant elliptical galaxy sits in the constellation Virgo — which galaxy is it?
Messier 87 (also known as Virgo A or NGC 4486, generally abbreviated to M87) is a supergiant elliptical galaxy in the constellation Virgo that contains several trillion stars.
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.
Concerned with the most fundamental concept of all — being — this branch of metaphysics distinguishes non-repeatable particulars from repeatable universals like 'green' — what is the field?
Ontology is the philosophical study of being.
Named after a 17th-century French mathematician and physicist, this SI unit of pressure is defined as one newton of force per square metre — name the unit?
Pascal (unit) (symbol: Pa) is the unit of pressure in the International System of Units (SI).
Prized as an ornamental indoor plant and still poorly understood taxonomically, this arum-family genus ranks second in size only to Anthurium — which genus?
Philodendron is a large genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae.
This category of polymer includes both natural proteins like wool and silk, and synthetic materials like nylon and aramid fibers — what is it?
Polyamide is a polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds.
This noncontagious autoimmune condition leaves dry, scaly patches of skin and can flare at the exact spot of an injury — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon; what is it?
Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.
This rapidly worsening brain condition can follow a bout of chickenpox or influenza and is strongly associated with aspirin use in children — what syndrome is it?
Reye syndrome is a rapidly worsening brain disease. Signs and symptoms of Reye syndrome may include vomiting, personality changes, confusion, seizures, and loss of consciousness.
A Stanford physicist who also held an English literature degree, in 1983 she became, at 32, the youngest American ever to fly in space. Who is she?
Sally Ride (May 26, 1951-July 23, 2012) was an American astronaut and physicist.

Drawing on tools from anthropology, biology, medicine, psychology, and criminology, this scientific field studies human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions, distinct from purely social commentary on the subject — what is this field called?
Sexology is the scientific study of human sexuality, including human sexual interests, behaviors, and functions.
This use of the human voice for language ranges from informing and persuading to simply asking or declaring, combining vowels and consonants into meaningful words — what is it called?
Speech is the use of the human voice as a medium for language.
Among the most experienced spacewalkers in history, this NASA astronaut logged over 62 hours across nine spacewalks — the most of any woman — who is she?
Sunita Williams (ne Pandya; born September 19, 1965) is a retired United States Navy captain and former NASA astronaut.
What academic discipline studies religious belief from within a faith perspective, focusing on the nature of divinity, revelation, and the history behind organized religion?
Theology is the study of religious belief from a religious perspective, with a focus on the nature of divinity and the history behind religion.
Named for the compulsive pulling of one's own hair, this disorder brings a brief positive feeling with each pull but is notoriously hard to stop — what is it?
Trichotillomania (TTM), also known as hair-pulling disorder or compulsive hair pulling, is a mental disorder characterized by a long-term urge that results in the pulling out of one's own hair.
This broad category of creative disciplines spans painting, sculpture, photography, and architecture, and includes applied fields like industrial and fashion design — what do we call it?
Visual arts are art forms such as painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, photography, video, image, filmmaking, design, crafts, and architecture.
This mosquito-borne viral disease causes chills, nausea, and muscle pain, and in about 15% of cases progresses to liver damage that turns the skin a telltale color — what disease is it?
Yellow fever is a viral disease of typically short duration.
This class of bony fish accounts for nearly 99% of all living fish species, ranging in size from an 8-millimeter minnow to a giant sunfish weighing 2,700 kilograms — what is it?
Actinopterygii: Class of ray-finned bony fishes.
Its very name comes from the Arabic for 'the kohl,' and chemically it's any compound carrying a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon — a family that ranges from methanol to cholesterol. What is it?
Alcohol (chemistry): Organic compound with at least one hydroxyl (–OH) group.
This functional group, formed by replacing a carboxylic acid's hydroxyl with an amino group, creates the peptide bonds that link amino acids into proteins — what is it?
Amide: Organic compounds of the form RC(=O)NR′R″.
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Pinned by a boulder in a Utah canyon in 2003, this mountaineer amputated his own forearm with a dull pocket knife to survive, later portrayed by James Franco in a film — who is he?
Delivered to the RAF starting in 1956, this delta-wing strategic bomber was considered the most advanced but riskiest of Britain's three V bombers — which aircraft?
Avro Vulcan: British jet-powered delta wing strategic bomber.
Nicknamed 'top shelf' dizziness, this inner-ear disorder causes brief spinning sensations lasting under a minute whenever you tilt or turn your head — what is this condition called?
Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo: Medical condition. Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), sometimes called "top shelf vertigo", is a disorder arising from a problem in the inner ear.

In this distributed ledger, each record holds a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so altering a single block would require rewriting every block that follows — making the data nearly tamper-proof. What is it?
Blockchain: Distributed data store for digital transactions.

Originating from feral Eastern Mediterranean populations, this single wild plant species has been cultivated into an astonishing range of vegetables including broccoli, cauliflower, kale, and Brussels sprouts. What is it?
Brassica oleracea: Species of plant. Brassica oleracea, also known as wild cabbage in its uncultivated form, is a plant of the family Brassicaceae.
The world's most widely consumed psychoactive substance works by mimicking adenosine's shape and blocking its receptors, keeping you awake — what is this stimulant?

This German-Swedish pharmacist had a knack for discovery — molybdenum, tungsten, barium, chlorine, and arguably oxygen all trace to his bench — but the same hands-on chemistry may have killed him via mercury poisoning. Which unlucky genius is it?
Carl Wilhelm Scheele: Swedish German chemist who discovered oxygen (1742–1786)
Descended from land mammals but now fully aquatic, this group swims via up-and-down tail strokes and includes toothed members capable of echolocation — what group includes whales and dolphins?
With about 3,400 species in over 520 genera, this insect family includes nearly every member of its group except two species in a small sister taxon — which family?
Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this plant genus produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and brewed into one of the world's most valuable traded commodities — which genus?
This group of RNA viruses, named for the club-shaped spikes that crown their surface, causes illnesses ranging from the common cold to SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 — what are they called?
Coronavirus: Subfamily of viruses in the family Coronaviridae.
Named after the bladder because it was first found in urine, this amino acid carries a thiol group that lets it forge the disulfide bonds holding many proteins together. Which amino acid is it?
Cysteine: Proteinogenic amino acid. Cysteine (symbol Cys or C) is a semiessential proteinogenic amino acid with the formula HS−CH2−CH(NH2)−COOH.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this is the sole species in its genus and lives in large, non-hierarchical clans with several breeding females — what's this wild canid called?
Dhole: Species of mammal. The dhole ( dohl; Cuon alpinus) is a canid native to South, East and Southeast Asia.

With nearly 24,000 ommatidia in each compound eye and wings usually held flat rather than folded, this iridescent flying insect is often confused with its lighter-bodied damselfly cousins — what is it?
The largest living land animal comes in three recognized species and counts mammoths and mastodons among its extinct cousins — what is it?
Elephant: Largest living land animal. The trunk is prehensile, bringing food and water to the mouth and grasping objects.
Marketed as Lexapro, this SSRI treats depression and anxiety but is exclusively sold commercially as an oxalate salt — what is it?

Escitalopram: SSRI antidepressant. It is mainly used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, obsessive–compulsive disorder (OCD), and social anxiety disorder.
With a black-tipped bushy tail and brownish-grey striped fur, this small wild feline lives in Scotland, Turkey, the Caucasus, and mainland forests, hunting rodents and ground birds — which species?
European wildcat: Small wild cat. The European wildcat (Felis silvestris) is a small wildcat species that was described in the late 18th century.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
Making up roughly 75% of antibodies found in the human bloodstream, which antibody type is produced by plasma B cells and features two paratopes?
A Harvard chemistry professor who studied chlorophyll and helped develop poison gas in WWI, he later became Harvard's president and the first U.S. ambassador to West Germany — who is he?
This New Zealand-American sexologist at Johns Hopkins coined the very phrases 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' — which controversial researcher is it?
John Money: New Zealand psychologist and sexologist (1921–2006)

With oversized heads, dagger-like bills, and stubby tails, these 118 brightly colored bird species swoop from perches to nab prey — and despite reputation, many don't even live near water — what family of birds?
Kingfisher: Family of birds. The family contains 118 species and is divided into three subfamilies and 19 genera.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented worms are mostly freshwater dwellers, and the medicinal species famously feeds on blood — what are they?
Leech: Parasitic or predatory annelid worms.
A Chinese computer engineer turned science-fiction author, he won the Hugo Award for The Three-Body Problem and the Locus Award for its sequel, Death's End. Who is he?
Liu Cixin: Chinese science fiction writer (born 1963)
Developed by MathWorks and named for its focus on matrix manipulations, this proprietary numeric computing environment powers the add-on Simulink for model-based design. What's it called?
MATLAB: Numerical computing environment and programming language.
Whether a milk board's 'Got Milk?' campaign or a city pitching itself as a tourist destination, this discipline boils down to acquiring, satisfying, and retaining customers — what is it?
Marketing: Study and process of exploring, creating, and delivering value to customers.
More than 80% of cases of this cancer — which grows in the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — trace back to asbestos exposure. What is it?

The only woman among Einstein's classmates at Zurich Polytechnic, this Serbian mathematician was his first wife and is still debated as a possible collaborator on his 1905 miracle-year papers. Who was she?
Mileva Marić: Wife of Albert Einstein (1875–1948)
With a pointed snout, round ears, and a scaly tail as long as its body, this small rodent species is usually distinguished from its larger cousin the rat mainly by size — which animal?
Mouse: Small long-tailed rodent. A mouse (pl. mice) is a small rodent, characteristically known to have a pointed snout, small rounded ears, a body-length scaly tail, and a high breeding rate.
Divided anatomically into vertebral, visceral, and two vascular compartments, which flexible body part connects the head to the torso and is also called the cervix or collum?
Neck: Body part that connects the head and torso. It supports the weight of the head and protects the nerves that transmit sensory and motor information between the brain and the rest of the body.
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
Mostly black on top, white below, and sporting unmistakable white eye patches, this cosmopolitan apex predator is actually the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family. What is it?
Orca: Largest living species of dolphin.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
Often triggered by a ruptured appendix or a perforated gallbladder, this inflammation of the abdominal lining causes severe pain and swelling — what is it?

Peritonitis: Inflammation of abdominal organ lining. Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
This Dutch experimental physicist shared the 1902 Nobel Prize with Hendrik Lorentz for discovering and explaining an effect that now bears his name — who was he?
Covered in sharp keratin quills for defense, this rodent's largest species ranks as the third-biggest living rodent in the world, behind only the capybara and the beaver. What animal is it?
Porcupine: Rodent with a coat of sharp spines.
Nicknamed 'gold cap' and 'golden halo,' this is the world's best-known psilocybin-containing mushroom thanks to its wide distribution and how easily it's cultivated — which species?
Psilocybe cubensis: Species of fungus. It belongs to the fungus family Hymenogastraceae and was previously known as Stropharia cubensis.
Also known as steelhead in its sea-run form, this North American Pacific species shows off a vivid reddish stripe along its flank in breeding males — which fish?
Rainbow trout: Fresh-water species of fish.
His 'Essai Sur La Nature Du Commerce' was called the 'cradle of political economy'; this Irish-French banker made a fortune speculating in John Law's Mississippi Company — who is it?
Richard Cantillon: Irish-French economist and banker (c. 1680 – 1734)
This light Swedish single-engine supersonic fighter has a delta wing and canard configuration with fly-by-wire controls and is fully NATO interoperable — what is it?
Saab JAS 39 Gripen: Light single-engined multirole fighter aircraft from Sweden.
Living on ocean floors worldwide, this leathery-skinned echinoderm recycles nutrients as a detritivore and is named for its resemblance to a common garden vegetable — what is it?

Also called carborundum, this hard compound occurs in nature as the rare mineral moissanite but has been mass-produced as an abrasive since 1893 — and it stiffens disc brakes and bulletproof vests; what is it?
Silicon carbide: Wide-bandgap semiconductor and abrasion-resistant ceramic.
Known by nicknames like 'garden' and 'lamb,' and native from Ireland to southern China, which herb's aromatic oil flavors food, teas, and various scents?
Spearmint: Plant species in the mint family.

Named from Greek words meaning 'a chain of berries' and 'pus-forming,' this Gram-positive bacterial species is the predominant carrier of the Lancefield group A antigen, often abbreviated GAS — what is this bacterium's full scientific name?
Streptococcus pyogenes: Species of bacterium. The name group A (beta-hemolytic) Streptococcus is thus also used.
These astringent polyphenolic compounds bind proteins and are found abundantly in oak bark, historically used to turn animal hides into leather — what are they?
Tannin: Class of astringent, bitter plant polyphenolic chemical compounds.
One of the three great clades of dinosaur, its members share hollow bones and three clawed toes per limb, were ancestrally carnivorous, and likely wore feathers in the Coelurosauria — which group?
